newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN THURSDAY TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN THURSDAY TRADE.

text.p: Zimbabwe's short-term money rates were quoted mixed in thin trade on Thursday, dealers said.
They said the Reserve Bank had offered Z$300 million worth of treasury bills to the market, but rejected all the bids, which came in above the benchmark rediscount rate, currently at 23.5 percent.

Market analysts say the Reserve Bank should increase the rediscount and pave the way for other money rates to go up in line with annual inflation, which rose to 22.4 percent in the year to April from 19.9 percent in March.
Meanwhile on Thursday, treasury bills were being traded on the secondary market unchanged at 22.75 percent, while call money added two percentage points to 20 percent.

NCD bills with 30-, 60- and 90-day maturities were quoted at 25 and 22 percent (buying and selling respectively) from 25 and 24 percent. Bank acceptance bills were being bought a percentage point lower at 24.25 percent and their selling rate eased to 23 percent from 23.5.
Reserve Bank figures showed the market closed on Wednesday with a surplus of Z$60.2 million.
